\textbf{(a)} By parts with $u=(\ln x)^2$, $dv=dx$ ($du=\frac{2\ln x}{x}dx$, $v=x$):
\[\int(\ln x)^2dx=x(\ln x)^2-2\int\ln x\,dx=\boxed{x(\ln x)^2-2x\ln x+2x+C}.\]
Again with $u=(\ln x)^3$:
\[\int(\ln x)^3dx=x(\ln x)^3-3\int(\ln x)^2dx=\boxed{x(\ln x)^3-3x(\ln x)^2+6x\ln x-6x+C}.\]
\textbf{(b)} Integrate by parts with $u=(\ln x)^k$, $dv=dx$. Then $du=k(\ln x)^{k-1}\cdot\frac1x\,dx$ and $v=x$, so
\[\int(\ln x)^kdx=x(\ln x)^k-\int x\cdot k(\ln x)^{k-1}\frac1x\,dx=x(\ln x)^k-k\int(\ln x)^{k-1}dx.\qquad\blacksquare\]
